newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - Still life in Australia 10-yr bond rally.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Still life in Australia 10-yr bond rally.

text.p: *The Australian 10-year bond futures contract struck an all time high of 93.640 on Thursday, but while this has proved a cap for the market, there is scope for the rally to continue.
*All eyes on RBA at 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) for possible policy easing after this week's benign inflation and wages data.

The Australian 10-year bond futures contract struck its highest level since being listed in 1984 at 93.640 on Thursday, but while this has proved a cap for the market for now, there is scope for the rally to continue on.

However, the market is showing some reluctance to push on into uncharted territory after taking out the previous high of 93.630 set early 1994, and ended the SYCOM session at 93.575 compared with Thursday's eventual pit close of 93.580.
"(Ten-year bonds) at multi-year highs is hardly an ideal place for aggressive new long positions," said Peter Pontikis, technical strategist at Westpac.

However, Pontikis added that he was not bearish at this stage, and with a high risk of a rate cut, and possibly another, this can only be read as affirming the broader uptrend, "even if Australian dollar bonds compress to parity to U.S.".

The 10-year bond yield differential to the U.S. made a strong test of 25 basis points on Thursday, its lowest level since the early 1980s following this week's benign inflation and wages data, which further strengthened hopes of a policy easing.
All eyes will be on the RBA at 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) for a possible policy announcement, although there are mixed opinions whether it will occur today or after the August board meeting.

A break of 93.640 could see the 10-year bond contract progress to 93.750, extending the rally since April to over 200 basis points. However, a breakdown of 94.470 would tarnish the market's bullish outlook.
September bill futures ended SYCOM at 94.98, equating to a cash rate of 5.02 percent, reflecting the strong expectations for a 50 basis points cut in current 5.5 percent official interest rates.
Meanwhile, U.S. Treasuries ended narrowly mixed amid a dearth of market moving news.
